D3's two supports are repository facts on record: `[tool.tach]` in pyproject.toml:33-38 declares only `tests.**.test_*` as modules and .agent-process/scripts/ci_check.py:155-162 states helper modules stay importable (the existing `from tests.publisher.delivery_fakes import ...` imports pass `tach check` today); the checkout root reaches sys.path through `python -m pytest`, which matters because `-c .agent-process/pyproject.toml` leaves rootdir at `.agent-process/` (ci_check.py:267-271) so its `pythonpath = ["."]` does not point at the checkout root — task 2.1 runs both configurations.

replaced.evidence: The replaced input is the interpreter path: `shutil.which("bash")` (environment PATH) becomes a path derived from `git --exec-path`. Failure modes are listed (design — Risks: a layout without `usr/bin/bash.exe`; D2: no PATH fallback, fail with the expected path, §IV). Both consumers are now listed: `TestPrePushHook._run`, and `test_missing_interpreter_fails_loudly`, whose lost proof D1 names — `Git\usr\bin` holds no `git.exe`, so the hook would exit 2 at `git rev-parse --local-env-vars` (.agent-process/.githooks/pre-push:6-9) before its interpreter loop and the test would still pass. Task 2.1 restores the proof: PATH becomes the bash directory plus the directory of `shutil.which("git")`, and the test asserts `pre-push: no supported Python interpreter found`, the hook's own line 27. That PATH excludes every candidate of the loop on both platforms (the `.venv/...` candidates are relative to the empty tmp tree; `py` lives in C:\Windows on Windows and does not exist on Linux), so the assertion fails if the run stops earlier.

catcher.evidence: D2's catcher is the helper's own assertion (the missing path, or the failed `git --exec-path` under `check=True`), reached as a test failure in every run of the two suites — tasks 2.1 and 2.2 locally, task 3.2's `python .agent-process/scripts/ci_check.py` (`==> pytest`, ci_check.py:265-273) and the same command on the pre-push route. The catcher for the consumer above is the stderr assertion of task 2.1, reached on every platform including Linux CI. On Linux the Windows branch of `git_bash()` is inert by design (design — Context), which is the defect's own scope.
